newsitem.title: USA: Hyatt purchases Miami hotel for $40.7 million.
newsitem.headline: Hyatt purchases Miami hotel for $40.7 million.

text.p: Hyatt Hotels Corp said Wednesday it purchased the Hyatt Regency Miami from Aetna Life Insurance Co of America for $40.7 million.
The purchase of the Hyatt Regency Miami is the first Florida purchase in the company's $1 billion expansion plan.
Hyatt currently operates four properties in South Florida.
Over the next three years, Hyatt has said it plans to acquire hotels and resorts throughout the United States, Caribbean and Canada with a special emphasis on Florida.

"We see a lot of opportunities in South Florida, not only in the domestic market but also as the gateway to Latin America," said Victor Lopez, divisional vice president Hyatt Hotels, in a news release.
The 615-room hotel has been managed by Hyatt since it was developed 1982. In 1995 the hotel underwent a $10 million renovation.

In the transaction, Hyatt purchased the Hyatt Regency Miami hotel facility and a long-term lease of the land on which the hotel sits. The land continues to be owned by the City of Miami. According to terms of the transaction, Hyatt said the fixed-based rent paid to Miami has been substantially increased.
Miami will will receive revenues in excess of $400,000 annually as a result of the sale.
Hyatt Hotels operates 105 hotels and resorts in the U.S., Canada and the Caribbean. Hyatt International, through its subsidiaries, operates 70 hotels and resorts in 33 countries.
